why: Part (a) is a correct value-by-value trace (sum 0.1, 0.4; 0.35<0.4 gives next=1), and in (b) the student does not merely re-trace the changed input (sums reach 0.9, r=0.95 never satisfied, next stays -1) but names the general condition under which the -1 sentinel appears — a row that does not sum to 1 — i.e. the class of inputs that exposes the failure, which goes beyond the given case to the conserved property the code relies on.
